Class 3 · Chapter 6 of 10

Time, timetables and dates

Read clocks to five minutes, work out time that crosses the hour and use dates.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Read scales and change units. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can read and choose clocks.
  • I can work out elapsed time.
  • I can use dates and timetables.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Count in fives

The numbers on a clock are 5 minutes apart.

When the long hand points to 5, it is 25 minutes past. This clock shows 3:25.

Screen 2 of 5

Minutes to the hour

After half past, we count the minutes to the next hour.

The long hand points to 10, so it is 10 minutes to 9.

Screen 3 of 5

Cross the hour

From 4:40 to 5:15: first jump to 5:00, then add 15 more minutes.

20 + 15 = 35 minutes.

Screen 4 of 5

Dates on a calendar

Days in the same row are 7 apart. The next row down is 7 days later.

April 7 and April 14 are both Tuesdays.

Screen 5 of 5

Read a timetable

A timetable gives start and end times. Find the gap between them.

The bus leaves at 8:15 and arrives at 8:50. 35 minutes of the hour are used and 25 are left.

Words to know
minutes past
Minutes since the hour, read on the right half of the clock.
minutes to
Minutes before the next hour, read on the left half of the clock.
timetable
A table that lists when things start and end.

For parents

What your child learns

1 hour is 60 minutes, so 6 hours 10 minutes is 6 × 60 + 10 = 370 minutes. 1 week is 7 days. To read a clock, read hours first, then minutes.

A common slip

Children often use 100 minutes in an hour. Remember 60. For days, divide by 7 and keep the remainder as days.

5-minute home activity: Time in parts

  1. Write 2 hours 30 minutes in minutes.
  2. Set a clock to 4:20 and say the hand positions.
  3. Count 80 days in groups of 7 on grid paper.
  4. Say the answer as weeks and days.
